newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CONFERENCE GROUP SEEKS S.AFRICAN SAFETY ASSURANCES.
newsitem.headline: CONFERENCE GROUP SEEKS S.AFRICAN SAFETY ASSURANCES.

text.p: A South African conference organiser said on Friday he had sought an assurance from President Nelson Mandela that concrete steps were being taken against violent crime.
"The critically important conference business sector is being threatened by violence which appears to be getting worse," Brian McDonald, managing director of Global Conferences, said in a statement.
"The situation is now so bad that many of our South African clients are having to reassure their international associations that it is still safe to hold conferences in South Africa."
He said South Africa's hosting of an international conference of medical specialists due to be held in 2001 was in jeopardy because of crime.

McDonald asked Mandela to provide assurances that the crime problem was being "vigorously addressed" in a bid to ensure the conference, which could bring in up to 15 million rand in foreign exchange, was held in South Africa.
